ties.applies_to: Governor and Lieutenant Governor, in the general election
ties.steps: if two or more sets of persons have the highest and equal number of votes for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, the Senate and House of Delegates choose one set by a joint majority viva voce; if two or more sets again have an equal number on a second vote confined to the tied sets, the election is determined by lot between those sets (Constitution, Art. II, sec. 4)
ties.who: the General Assembly (Senate and House of Delegates), then a lot if the vote is again equal

sources.quote: If two or more sets of persons shall have the highest and equal number of votes for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, one set of them shall be chosen Governor and Lieutenant Governor, by the Senate and House of Delegates
if the vote should again be equal, then the election of Governor and Lieutenant Governor shall be determined by lot between those sets

ties.note: Md. Const. Art. II, sec. 4. The PDF is the Department of Legislative Services' 2015 print of the Constitution; amendments after 1 January 2015 are not in it.

ties.steps: the returns go to the Governor, whose duty it is to decide on the election and qualification of the person returned and, in case of a tie between two or more persons, to designate which of them shall qualify as Attorney General (Constitution, Art. V, sec. 2)

sources.quote: in case of a tie between two or more persons, to designate which of said persons shall qualify as Attorney General

ties.note: Md. Const. Art. V, sec. 2. The Constitution gives the Governor the designation; it does not say by what method (a lot is not named).

ties.applies_to: Comptroller (the other statewide office chosen by the voters; the Treasurer is chosen by the General Assembly)
ties.steps: if at any election directed by the Constitution two or more candidates have the highest and an equal number of votes, a new election is ordered by the Governor, except in cases specially provided for by the Constitution (Art. XVII, sec. 8)
ties.who: the Governor orders; the voters decide

sources.quote: If at any election directed by this Constitution, any two or more candidates shall have the highest and an equal number of votes, a new election shall be ordered by the Governor, except in cases specially provided for by this Constitution.

ties.note: Md. Const. Art. XVII, sec. 8. That the Comptroller (Art. VI, sec. 1: "a Comptroller chosen by the qualified electors of the State") is an office at "an election directed by this Constitution" is a reading, not a statement; the section does not name offices.

ties.applies_to: Senator and Delegate, in the general election
ties.steps: in case of a tie between two or more such qualified persons, the Governor appoints a person to fill the vacancy from the name submitted in writing within 30 days by the central committee of the political party (Constitution, Art. III, sec. 13(a)(1)); if no name is submitted the Governor appoints a person of the same party (13(a)(2)); in a district of two or more counties each county's central committee has one vote and, on a tie between the committees, the list of names is submitted and the Governor chooses from it (13(b)(3))
ties.who: the party central committee proposes; the Governor appoints

sources.quote: or in case of a tie between two or more such qualified persons, the Governor shall appoint a person to fill such vacancy from a person whose name shall be submitted to him in writing, within thirty days after the occurrence of the vacancy, by the Central Committee of the political party

ties.note: Md. Const. Art. III, sec. 13(a)(1). The section is about vacancies in the offices of Delegate or Senator and names a tie among persons "chosen as a Delegate or Senator" as a case of vacancy; the appointee must be of the party of the vacating member 'at the last election', which the text does not tie to the candidates in a tie [read as the clause is written]. This is the specific provision to which Art. XVII, sec. 8 (new election) gives way ('except in cases specially provided').

ties.steps: the returns go to the judges having criminal jurisdiction, whose duty it is to decide upon the elections and qualifications of the persons returned and, in case of a tie between two or more persons, to designate which of them shall qualify as State's Attorney (Constitution, Art. V, sec. 8)
ties.who: the judges of the circuit court having criminal jurisdiction

sources.quote: in case of a tie between two or more Persons, to designate which of said persons shall qualify as State’s Attorney

ties.applies_to: member of an elective local board of education, in the general election
ties.steps: if two or more nominees tie for the last office to be filled, the office is considered vacant and is filled as if the vacancy occurred during the term, by the selection of one of the nominees who tie in the general election (Election Law 8-806(b)(2)); how the selection is made is left to the Education Article, which was not read
ties.who: the authority that fills a board of education vacancy under the Education Article (not read)

sources.quote: If two or more nominees each receive the lowest number of votes necessary to qualify for election, creating a tie for the last office to be filled, the office shall be considered vacant.
by the selection of one of the nominees who ties in the general election.

ties.note: Election Law 8-806(b)(2). Applies to boards of education without party designation; 8-806 does not apply where Title 3 of the Education Article requires a partisan election (8-802(b)).

ties.applies_to: other county offices elected by the voters (county commissioners, county council and the like), in the general election
ties.steps: a new election is ordered by the Governor if two or more candidates have the highest and an equal number of votes at an election directed by the Constitution (Art. XVII, sec. 8)
ties.who: the Governor orders; the voters decide

sources.quote: If at any election directed by this Constitution, any two or more candidates shall have the highest and an equal number of votes, a new election shall be ordered by the Governor, except in cases specially provided for by this Constitution.

ties.note: Md. Const. Art. XVII, sec. 8 and the purpose clause of sec. 1 of the Article ("all State and county elections"). That it covers county councils and commissioners is a reading; county charters (Art. XI-A) and local laws were not read.

ties.applies_to: a primary for an office that is entirely in one county
ties.steps: a nominee who "gains a tie vote with another candidate in a primary election" creates a vacancy in nomination, filled by the central committee of the party; the nominee the committee selects must be one of the tied candidates (Election Law 5-1004(b)(1), (c), (d))
ties.who: the party's central committee (the county's, or the legislative district's committee where the central committee is elected by district)

sources.quote: If a nominee for an office that is entirely in one county declines the nomination or gains a tie vote with another candidate in a primary election, the vacancy in nomination shall be filled by the 88th day before the general election.
If the vacancy results because of a tie vote between two or more candidates, the nominee selected by the central committee under this section shall be one of those candidates.

ties.note: Election Law 5-1004. The statewide and multi-county offices are in 5-1002 and 5-1003, which name death, declination and disqualification as the causes of a vacancy and do not mention a tie in a primary (see the next rule).

ties.applies_to: a primary for a statewide office or an office whose district includes more than one county (Representative in Congress, State Senator, Delegate)
ties.steps: no provision for a tie in such a primary was found
ties.note: Read: Election Law Title 5, subtitle 10 (5-1001 to 5-1005) and subtitle 9 (5-901 and following), and a search of the whole Election Law article for 'tie', 'tied', 'equal number', 'same number of votes' and 'lot'. 5-1002 (statewide office) and 5-1003 (district of more than one county) name death, declination and disqualification only. Regulations (COMAR) were not read, so a rule there is not excluded.

ties.applies_to: a primary for an elective local board of education (nonpartisan)
ties.steps: if two or more candidates tie for the last nomination, each of them is a nominated candidate (Election Law 8-804(c)(2))
ties.who: no drawing or vote: every tied candidate is nominated

sources.quote: If two or more candidates each receive the lowest number of votes necessary to qualify for nomination, creating a tie for the last nomination for the office to be filled, each shall be a nominated candidate.

ties.note: Election Law 8-804(c)(2); the candidates equal in number to twice the offices to be filled are nominated.

ties.applies_to: U.S. Senator, Representative in Congress and presidential electors, in the general election
ties.steps: no provision for a tie was found
ties.note: Read: Election Law 11-601 (the Governor declares elected the electors, and the member of Congress, who receive the highest number of votes), Title 11 subtitles 3 to 6 (canvass and certification) and a search of the whole Election Law article for the words of a tie. Art. XVII, sec. 8 of the Constitution speaks of an election "directed by this Constitution"; whether a federal election is one was not decided. A tie for Congress is also within each chamber's power to judge its members (U.S. Constitution, not read).

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for those candidates (the apparent winner and the losing candidate with the highest number of votes for the office)
threshold.in_words: a defeated candidate for public or party office may petition for a recount if the margin between the apparent winner and the leading loser is not more than 5% of the votes cast for those two

who_may_request: a candidate for public or party office who has been defeated on the certified results, by petition filed within 3 days after the results are certified; an opposing candidate may file a counterpetition if the petition did not cover all the precincts and the winner changes
recounts.cost_bearer: the petitioner, whose bond is liable (the cost is the county's if the margin was 0.25% or less, the outcome changed, or the petitioner gained 2% or more)

sources.quote: a candidate for public or party office who has been defeated based on the certified results of any election conducted under this article may petition for a recount of the votes cast for the office sought.

A candidate may not petition for a recount if the margin of difference between the number of votes received by an apparent winner and the losing candidate with the highest number of votes for the office is greater than 5% of the total votes cast for those candidates.

recounts.note: Election Law 12-101 (petition) with 12-102 (counterpetition), 12-105 (bond set by a circuit judge) and 12-107 (cost). The section covers "any election conducted under this article"; the kinds list follows that wording [inferred for presidential electors, not named]. The petitioner chooses the method (rescan, manual recount of voter-verifiable paper records, or another method the State Administrator approves) under 12-108. There is no automatic recount in the article (searched).

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for those candidates
threshold.in_words: at a margin of 0.25% or less a recount costs the petitioner nothing: the county pays

who_may_request: the petitioning candidate, as in the rule above
recounts.cost_bearer: the county, in which the recount is held

sources.quote: the margin of difference in the number of votes received by an apparent winner and the losing candidate with the highest number of votes for an office is 0.25% or less of the total votes cast for those candidates
If the petitioner is not liable for the costs of the recount as provided in subsection (b) of this section, a county shall pay the costs of the recount in that county.

recounts.note: Election Law 12-107(b)(2)(iii)1. and (c). Beyond 0.25% the petitioner pays unless the outcome changes or the petitioner gains 2% or more of the total votes cast for the office in all precincts being recounted (12-107(b)(2)(i) and (ii)): quote of the general rule: "each petitioner shall pay the cost of a recount requested under this subtitle and the petitioner's bond is liable for the cost".

recounts.election: any election with a question on the ballot

threshold.percent_of: the votes cast for and against the question (the margin between the votes for and the votes against, as a percentage)
threshold.in_words: a registered voter eligible to vote on a ballot question may petition for a recount unless the margin between the votes for and against is greater than 5%; the county pays if the margin is 0.25% or less

who_may_request: a registered voter eligible to vote for the question, by petition filed within 3 days after the results are certified (in the county if the question was on the ballot in one county, with the State Board if in more than one)
recounts.cost_bearer: the petitioner, whose bond is liable, unless the margin is 0.25% or less, the outcome changes, or the petitioner gains 2% or more; then the county

sources.quote: a petition for a recount based on the certified results of a question on the ballot in an election conducted under this article may be filed by a registered voter eligible to vote for that question.
A registered voter may not file a petition for a recount if the margin of difference between the number of votes cast for and the number of votes cast against the question is greater than 5%.

recounts.note: Election Law 12-103 and 12-104 (counterpetition) and 12-107(b)(2)(iii)2. (the question's margin is 0.25% or less). The 5% is stated as a margin of the votes for and against; the section does not say 5% of what total.

unread.what: county charters and local laws (county councils, county executives, municipalities) for tie rules and recounts; COMAR regulations on recounts; the Education Article on filling a board of education vacancy; the Maryland Constitution after 1 January 2015
unread.reason: not read; state general law only, and the Constitution PDF on the site is the 2015 print

notes: Maryland's Election Law article has no tie-break for a general election for Congress, the electors or the legislature; ties are in the Constitution (Governor and Lieutenant Governor by the General Assembly with a lot as the last step; Attorney General by the Governor; Delegates and Senators by the party central committee and the Governor; other officers by a new election ordered by the Governor) and in a few Election Law sections (primary for a one-county office by the party central committee; boards of education).
Maryland has no automatic recount: every recount is on the petition of a candidate (or, for a question, of a registered voter) at a margin of 5% or less, free at 0.25% or less.
